match.reason: None of the bank points teaches how to cite a source by naming author, title and date in the text and a reference list; the closest, eng-punctuation-quoting-citing, covers quotation punctuation and only briefly mentions citation, and the rest are about source reliability, intertextuality or style.

draft.title: Citing sources
card: A citation names where a writer's information or ideas came from. It gives credit to the person who made them.
a short note placed beside the borrowed idea, usually the author's name and the year, such as (Nguyen, 2021).
a list at the end of the work. Each entry gives the author, the title and the date, and sometimes more details such as the publisher or web address.
Citing lets readers check the source for themselves. A writer who uses someone else's work without naming it is passing it off as their own.
draft.remember: Cite to give credit and to let readers find the source.

a.q: Why does a writer put a reference list at the end of an essay?
opts: So readers can find and check the sources used
So the essay reaches the required word count
So the writer can avoid using quotation marks
So the teacher knows how long research took
a.why: A reference list gives the author, title and date of each source, so a reader can find it and check it. It does not change the length of the work or replace marking the borrowed words in the text.
a.clue: Think about what a reader can do with the list.

b.q: Priya's report on coral reefs uses a statistic from an article by Tom Hale, published in 2022. She puts the statistic in her own words. What should she do?
opts: Add (Hale, 2022) in the text and list the article at the end
Add nothing, because the sentence is in her own words
List the article at the end only if she copied it exactly
Add (Priya, 2022) in the text so readers know who wrote it
b.why: The idea and statistic came from Hale, so Priya needs to credit him, even though the wording is hers. She names him in the text and gives full details in the reference list. Rewording does not remove the need to cite.
b.clue: Does changing the words change who the idea came from?

a.best: So readers can find and check the sources used

b.best: Add (Hale, 2022) in the text and list the article at the end
